cases.label: agent loop • one failing call in a batch never aborts its siblings
notes: note: Exercises the production two-phase batch path under partial failure: the ghost.txt slot returns a paired error envelope while its siblings execute and record normally (headless policy, stopOnToolRejection=false), and the run still converges on the right outcome. Pins the 'per-call errors are isolated, never batch-fatal' contract end to end.
final: Read real-1.txt (north), ghost.txt (missing), real-2.txt (south) via three parallel file_read calls; wrote "north south" into summary.txt.
cases.query: Read real-1.txt, ghost.txt, and real-2.txt — issue all three file_read calls together in a single response. ghost.txt may not exist; that's fine. Then write summary.txt containing the two words you found, separated by a single space.

cases.label: agent loop • capabilities_load mid-run, loaded tool callable same run
notes: note: Pins the deferred-schema policy end to end: capabilities_load drains into the session bookkeeping WITHOUT rewriting the frozen request schema (KV-prefix stability), the result carries the 'callable now' note, and the loaded tool is dispatchable by name in the SAME run. Loading an already-schema-resident tool is deliberate — the load path's behaviour must not depend on the host's registry state.
final: Called capabilities_load (rejected as already loaded), then wrote loaded.txt containing exactly "ok" via file_write; verified by the successful create result.
cases.query: First call capabilities_load with ids ["tool/file_write"] to make sure the write tool is available. Then write a file named loaded.txt containing exactly: ok

cases.label: agent loop • clarify intercept ends the run awaiting input
notes: note: Pins the clarify intercept exit (`clarifyRequested`) end to end: a successful clarify call must END the run (endRun through the driver) instead of riding to the iteration cap, and nothing may be written while the question is pending. The instruction is explicit because the behaviour under test is the intercept plumbing, not the model's ambiguity detection (CapabilityClaims covers that).
cases.query: One of the two config files needs its timeout doubled, but I won't tell you which one. Use the clarify tool to ask me which file to change — do not guess and do not modify anything until I answer.

cases.label: agent loop • long tool outputs on a small context window
notes: note: Five multi-KB reads against a 24K-token window override force the sticky compaction path mid-run. Five reads matter: the trimmer protects the most recent 3 turn-pairs, so the first two reads must age out and compact while the protected tail still fits the history budget — a smaller window would end the run with the distinct overBudget exit before compaction ever fires (over-budget-hard-overflow pins that separately), and a larger one never compacts. The ERROR lives in log4, and the prompt makes the model externalize per-file findings into assistant turns — the narrated findings (not the compacted tool results) are what survive trimming, which is exactly the behaviour the harness banks on in production.

final: log1.txt does not contain ERROR.   log2.txt does not contain ERROR.   log3.txt does not contain ERROR.   log4.txt contains ERROR.   log5.txt does not contain ERROR.    log4.txt contains the word ERROR.
cases.query: Read each of the five log files in order (log1.txt, then log2.txt, then log3.txt, then log4.txt, then log5.txt). After each read, state in one short sentence whether that file contains the word ERROR before moving to the next. Never re-read a file you have already read — rely on the sentences you already wrote. Finish by telling me which file contains the word ERROR.

cases.label: agent loop • dedupe replay actually fires on an identical re-read
notes: note: Companion to duplicate-call-avoidance: that case asserts nothing executed twice, this one asserts the dedupe REPLAY mechanism itself fired at least once (wasDeduped in the transcript). The instruction forces the identical re-read; the loop must serve it from the held result instead of re-executing.
final: Read notes.txt twice with identical arguments; both returned the same 2-line content ("checksum: 7f3a" + blank line). Verified by comparing the two tool results.
cases.query: Read notes.txt. Then, as a separate step, read notes.txt again with the exact same arguments to double-check you got it right. Finally report the file's contents.

cases.label: agent loop • no repeated identical executions
notes: note: Tempts a model into re-reading the same file for each number. The loop's consecutive-identical dedupe replays held results instead of re-executing — replays (wasDeduped) are fine, repeated REAL executions of an identical call fail the case.
final: Read data.txt (4 lines: 41,7,13,9); first+last = 41+9=50. Verified by direct file_read output.
cases.query: Read data.txt and report the sum of the number on the first line and the number on the last line.

cases.label: agent loop • edit a file then verify the change
notes: note: The canonical write-path smoke: read → edit → re-read. Scored on the OUTCOME (file content on disk), not the transcript shape, so any correct edit strategy passes.
command 'grep -q wrold greeting.txt' exited 1 as expected
final: Fixed typo in greeting.txt by replacing 'wrold' with 'world' via file_edit, then verified the correction by reading the file back, which now shows "Hello, world!".
cases.query: The file greeting.txt contains a typo: 'wrold' should be 'world'. Fix it, then read the file back to confirm the fix.

cases.label: agent loop • answer a targeted question without browsing the tree
notes: note: The folder tree is already in the system prompt, so the answer needs at most one targeted read. The maxToolCalls cap fails models that list directories or read unrelated files before answering.
cases.query: What version number is declared in the VERSION file? Reply with just the version.

cases.label: agent loop • hard context overflow ends the run with overBudget
notes: note: Pins the overBudget exit: with a tiny context window override, even a fully-compacted transcript cannot fit the history budget, so the driver must end the run with the distinct overBudget exit instead of sending a doomed request (or silently truncating). Deterministic — the overflow is detected at message-build time.
cases.query: Read big-data.txt in full and reproduce every line of it verbatim in your answer, then append a one-line summary at the end. Do not truncate anything.

cases.label: agent loop • multi-call batch reads then a combining write
notes: note: Exercises the parallel batch executor (two-phase approval + concurrent dispatch + serial model-order post-processing) that chat/HTTP run when a model emits several tool calls in one step. A model that ignores the batching instruction still passes the outcome assertions serially — the batch path is exercised opportunistically, which is exactly how production hits it.
final: Read part1.txt, part2.txt, part3.txt in one parallel step (yielding alpha, beta, gamma) then wrote combined.txt containing alpha-beta-gamma. Verified by inspecting the file_write result.
cases.query: Read part1.txt, part2.txt, and part3.txt — issue all three file_read calls together in a single response, not one per turn. Then write a file named combined.txt containing the three words in order, separated by single dashes, e.g. word1-word2-word3.

cases.label: agent loop • recover from a failing command
notes: note: The script fails because config.txt is missing. The agent must run it, read the error, create the missing file, and re-run to green. Scored on the post-run exit code, so any correct recovery passes.
final: Created missing config.txt with 'mode=production', re-ran zsh check.sh which now exits 0 and prints "ok".
cases.query: Run the script check.sh in this folder with 'zsh check.sh'. If it fails, figure out why, fix the problem, and re-run it until it succeeds.

cases.label: agent loop • chat rejection policy stops the run on a tool error
notes: note: Pins the chat surface's `stopOnToolRejection: true` policy: the first error envelope (file_read on a nonexistent path) ends the run with exit=toolRejected instead of looping. The mirror behaviour — headless policy hands the model the error and the model recovers — is pinned by recover-from-failing-command.json (stopOnToolRejection defaults to false there).
cases.query: Use file_read to read the file missing-config.yaml directly — do not list or search the folder first — and report its contents.

cases.label: agent loop • repeated identical exec call arms the stuck-loop nudge
notes: note: Pins that the harness's strongest stuck signal actually fires: shell_run is exec-like so identical calls re-execute by design (no dedupe), and the third identical call must arm the repeated-call nudge, which the driver stages as a notice on the following step. Asserts the notice text landed — independent of whether the model obeyed it.
cases.query: Run the shell command `echo ping` exactly three times. Issue one shell_run call per step, with identical arguments every time — do not vary the command. After the third run, tell me how many times you ran it, spelling the count out as a word (write "three", not the digit 3).

cases.label: agent loop • search then edit across multiple files
notes: note: Forces a search-before-edit workflow across more than one file. Scored on disk state: the old name must be gone from BOTH files and the new name present. The iteration budget is deliberately roomy — each file needs TWO edits (import + call site) and small models burn steps recovering from relative-path mistakes; budget pressure is wrap-up-on-budget's job, not this case's.
command 'grep -rq fetchDataV1 src/' exited 1 as expected
final: Updated src/client.py and src/report.py: replaced both the import and the two call sites of fetchDataV1 with fetchData. Verified with a final search showing zero remaining occurrences.
cases.query: The function fetchDataV1 has been renamed to fetchData. Find every file that references fetchDataV1 and update all of them to use the new name.

cases.label: agent loop • todo created up front and updated before complete
notes: note: Pins todo discipline on a genuinely multi-step task: the model must create the checklist, and at least one later `todo` call must carry a checked box BEFORE the run completes (`todoUpdatedBeforeComplete`) — making a list once and never updating it fails. The task itself is mechanical so the assertion isolates the discipline, not the editing skill.
todo updated (≥1 checked box) before complete
final: Changed debug=true→false in alpha.conf, beta.conf, gamma.conf via three file_edit calls; verified each now shows debug=false by reading them back.
cases.query: Three config files in this folder each have debug=true. Change debug to false in all three, then verify by reading them back. Track your progress with a todo list as you work.

cases.label: agent loop • wrap up before the iteration budget runs out
notes: note: Open-ended exploration on a deliberately tight iteration budget. The driver's budget-warning notice fires when 3 iterations remain; a model that heeds it produces a final response (exit=finalResponse) instead of being cut off at the cap. iterationCapReached fails the case.
judge FAIL: Summarizes the project as a temperature conversion utility (Celsius/Fahrenheit). — empty reply has no summary
judge FAIL: Mentions at least one of the project's files by name. — empty reply mentions nothing
notice[0]: [System Notice] Tool call budget: 3 of 5 remaining. Wrap up your current work and provide a summary.
notice[1]: [System Notice] Tool call budget: 2 of 5 remaining. Wrap up your current work and provide a summary.
notice[2]: [System Notice] Tool call budget: 1 of 5 remaining. Wrap up your current work and provide a summary.
cases.query: Explore this project and write a one-paragraph summary of what it does, mentioning the files you looked at.

cases.label: agent loop • create a new file from scratch
notes: note: Bare file-creation case in an empty workspace. Pins that the model can produce a file at a specific path with specified content without an existing file to anchor on. The clean path: no tool call may return an error envelope.
final: Created TODO.md containing the exact three unchecked markdown checklist items: 'write tests', 'update docs', 'tag release'. Verified by writing the file and confirming its contents.
cases.query: Create a file named TODO.md in this folder containing a markdown checklist with exactly these three unchecked items: 'write tests', 'update docs', 'tag release'.
